# WingFoil

> A structured harness for AI-assisted software development, built to make it deterministic, a goal it measures: it keeps a project's memory, DNA, directives and workflows in git, and serves them to humans and AI agents through a CLI and an MCP server.

## Docs

- [User guide](https://wingfoil.github.io/wingfoil/docs/user-guide.md): Step-by-step guide to configuring and using WingFoil in your own project, from `wingfoil init` to connecting an AI agent.
- [CLI reference](https://wingfoil.github.io/wingfoil/docs/cli-reference.md): Every `wingfoil` command, one entry each: arguments, options, exit codes and output.
- [Guide for AI agents](https://wingfoil.github.io/wingfoil/docs/agents.md): For an agent working in a project that uses WingFoil: how to read the project and change it without breaking its rules.
- [Examples](https://wingfoil.github.io/wingfoil/docs/examples/README.md): Runnable, self-checking scripts, one per scenario, each printing the real output of every command it runs.

## Optional

- [API reference](https://wingfoil.github.io/wingfoil/api/): The TypeScript API of the `wingfoil` package, generated by TypeDoc.
- [Comparison](https://wingfoil.github.io/wingfoil/docs/comparison.md): WingFoil beside agent-rule files, spec-driven development tools, coding agents and IDEs, each fact about another tool with its source and the date it was read.
- [Case study: WingFoil develops WingFoil](https://wingfoil.github.io/wingfoil/docs/case-study.md): How this repository governs itself with WingFoil, and the release-health figures measured at v0.1 and v0.2, with what is not measurable yet.
- [Changelog](https://wingfoil.github.io/wingfoil/CHANGELOG.md): Release notes, one section per published version.
